uncertain_points.claim: The purpose of the specific 5-bit encodings for mux4_sel_e (MUX4_SEL_0 = 5'b01110, MUX4_SEL_1 = 5'b11000, MUX4_SEL_2 = 5'b00001, MUX4_SEL_3 = 5'b10111) is not documented; the encodings appear to provide a minimum Hamming distance of 3, which may be intended for fault tolerance, but this is not stated.
uncertain_points.cond: always, when the enum type is used
uncertain_points.risk: Future modifications could inadvertently reduce the Hamming distance, allowing a single- or double-bit fault to produce another valid select value, defeating the intended fault-tolerance property if one exists.

uncertain_points.claim: The enum mux4_sel_e defines only 4 legal values out of 32 possible 5-bit encodings; any other 5-bit value represents a legal but unlisted encoding in the type.
uncertain_points.cond: when a variable of type mux4_sel_e is used in synthesis or simulation without exhaustive case coverage
uncertain_points.risk: If downstream RTL uses a case statement with this enum and no default, unlisted values could lead to simulation X-propagation or synthesis don't-care optimization, potentially allowing an undefined mux select in the presence of bit errors.

uncertain_points.claim: Modules that instantiate a 4-to-1 mux using mux4_sel_e must handle all legal and illegal encodings explicitly; the package does not enforce any default value or coverage.
uncertain_points.cond: when mux4_sel_e is used as a select signal in combinational or sequential logic
uncertain_points.risk: Missing default or an incomplete case could introduce simulation/synthesis mismatches and break security assumptions about mux selection integrity.
